promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, 2 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You ran last week exactly as planned, and you don't need the 22-miler. Sunday's 16 miles with 8 at marathon pace is your last big run before the taper.

flags.title: Marathon-pace discipline
flags.detail: Run Sunday's 8 race-pace miles at 8:30–8:40/mi. Going faster adds fatigue two weeks out and practises the wrong race-day rhythm.

flags.title: Heart rate on race-pace miles

flags.title: No catch-up miles
flags.detail: The new date takes away two build weeks, and extra runs or reps won't give them back. Run the plan as written, as you have for the last two weeks.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No. Skip the 22-miler. There isn't room for it, and you don't need it.

Your 20 on Sep 13 and your 17 last Sunday give you enough long-run base for a 3:45. At your long-run pace, 22 miles would take about 3h40m. That's well past the 2.5 to 3 hours where long runs pay off. It would also land two weeks before the race, and you'd need more than two weeks to recover from it.

Instead, you get Sunday's 16 miles with 8 at marathon pace, which takes about 2.5 hours. It's closer to race day than 22 easy miles, and you'll still be fresh for the taper.

| Week | Miles | Long run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sep 28 – Oct 4 | about 39 | 16 mi with 8 at marathon pace |
| Oct 5 – 11 | about 30 | 12 mi easy |
| Oct 12 – 18 | about 15 before race day | the race, 26.2 mi |

Moving the race up costs you two build weeks, not the fitness you already have.

new.analysis:
**Last week went exactly to plan.** Every run matched its planned distance, from the easy days to the 17-mile long run, for 42 miles. That's two weeks in a row on plan, after the week of Sep 7 ran 15 miles over.

**Your sessions show fitness that fits a 3:45.** You held 7:58/mi across three 2-mile threshold reps with only 1% fade. Your easy runs stay near 9:50/mi at about 138 bpm. Marathon pace usually sits 30 to 40 seconds per mile slower than threshold, and 8:35/mi falls inside that range.

**Your endurance is in place.** Last Sunday's 17 miles held 9:49–10:02/mi from start to finish, and heart rate rose only 4.7 bpm. Flat splits that late in a long run are what you want three weeks out.

**This week is the last solid one, and it swaps distance for race pace.** Volume eases slightly to about 39 miles. The threshold work drops from 6 miles to 4.5 so you're fresher for Sunday, the closest thing to race day in the whole build.

**Expect less of the week to show as easy running, probably 60 to 69 percent.** With two quality days, warm-ups, recoveries and race-pace miles all count toward the harder zones. Every other run stays under 145 bpm, which is the right balance for this stage.

**From here, rest helps your race more than extra miles.** Training in the last two weeks adds little fitness by race day, but you'll still feel any extra fatigue from it. Keep your usual strength routine at a light load and add nothing new.
